title: Make 24 From Four Cards

concept.title: Pick two numbers, replace them by one result, and repeat
body: Four cards with numbers from 1 to 9: can you reach **24** using each card exactly once, the operations `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and brackets? Brackets decide which two numbers are combined first. Instead of thinking about brackets, use a simple recursion: **choose two numbers from the list, combine them with one operation, and put the result back** in the list. The list becomes shorter by one. When one number remains, check if it is 24.

Trying **every ordered pair** `(i, j)` covers `x - y` and `y - x`, and `x / y` and `y / x`. Division produces fractions (`8 / (3 - 8 / 3) = 24`), so the numbers are real numbers, and the final check uses a small tolerance because decimal results are not exact. Avoid dividing by zero. With four cards there are at most a few thousand combinations to try.

statement: You have four cards with integers from 1 to 9. Using each card exactly once, the operations `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` (real division) and any brackets, can you get exactly 24? Print `yes` or `no`.
inputFormat: The only line has the four integers.
hints: Pick an ordered pair of numbers, apply each operation, and recurse on the shorter list.
Division can give fractions: use real numbers and compare with a tiny tolerance.
